clauses.title: The post-push state is defined for every push, not only the first
requires: `WORKSPACE_POST_PUSH(C, O)` := public/workspace `C`, the no-replace sole child of the public head `P` it was pushed onto (`O` for the run's first push), with clean state; linked permits only a remote-tracking chain from `O` to `C` that the helper verifies as sole-child ancestry, through the heads `build_operator_revalidate` derives from the run's own post-push snapshots (CL-D79, CL-D86), clone operator stays `O`.

clauses.title: The invocation map names the chain a later push passes
requires: After an earlier push in the same run, linked also passes `priorPushHeads`, the heads it pushed before `C`, oldest first; the chain from `O` to `C` must run through only those heads, each the sole child of the one before, at most five in all (CL-D79).

clauses.title: The post-push invariant admits a sole-child chain of pushes
requires: After an earlier push in the same run, linked also passes `priorPushHeads`, the heads it pushed before `C`, oldest first; the chain from `O` to `C` must run through only those heads, each the sole child of the one before, at most five in all (CL-D79).

clauses.title: The residual CL-D86 leaves on the post-push chain
requires: A linear child someone else pushed still passes the helper if the run's snapshots name it, a residual of CL-D79 this decision does not remove.

clauses.title: README names every push before the current one
requires: with `priorPushHeads` naming every head the run pushed before `C`, oldest first, derived by `build_operator_revalidate` from the run's own post-push snapshots (CL-D79, CL-D86)

clauses.title: CL-D79 records the chain the post-push guard accepts
clauses.section: ## CL-D79 — The post-push guard accepts a sole-child chain of pushes
requires: issues/140#issuecomment
`priorPushHeads`
at most five
Re-capturing the baseline after a push, or binding every chain head to a packaged record of the run's pushes, requires a new owner decision
issues/140#issuecomment-5742362840
The guard proves ancestry, not who pushed: any chain meeting those conditions passes it, whoever pushed it
issues/140#issuecomment-5742591079
bind only the current head to the run's own workspace
a known residual, not a defect

clauses.title: The chain rule is pinned by its own regression
requires: Issue #140 a second pushed correction is accepted when the run names the first
Issue #140 the chain reaches the five-push cap and no further
Issue #140 a chain that leaves out, reorders, or starts past a head is refused
Issue #140 a merge anywhere in the chain is refused
Issue #140 the chain must end at the tracking ref and be well formed
Issue #140 the builder carries priorPushHeads beside postPushHead and refuses it otherwise
Issue #140 the packaged CLI carries the chain from the builder to the guard
